title: Drive the native Galaxy to System LOD bridge from the continuous wheel coordinate

scope.subject: Reuse the merged pinned-YEIS native system LOD bridge and the existing System-to-Surface continuous-scale coordinator so every wheel/trackpad delta directly advances or reverses Galaxy=0 to System=1 instead of launching a time-driven native autopilot.

research_summary: PR #81 restored the correct pinned-YEIS point-to-native-system LOD chain, reference-frame switch, shared physical-system span and matched System handoff, but its first Galaxy inward wheel still launches CameraController autopilot and completes 0→1 as a time-driven travel. The existing product scale coordinator already proves the required input contract on System=1 through Surface=5: each wheel/trackpad delta mutates one normalized coordinate immediately, semantic phases are only boundary labels, and reverse input evaluates the same path backward. The reuse-first change is therefore not another renderer or camera: retain #81's native BodyRenderer/BodyPoints/OrbitLines and frame switch, retain the product coordinator's delta normalization, and expose a narrow YEIS native scale-progress executor that places the existing CameraController along the same focus-relative logarithmic distance curve as the restored system LOD. At coordinate 1, reuse #81's matched native System overview and entry quaternion; on reverse, retain its view state and evaluate the same coordinate back toward the captured Galaxy anchor.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS CameraController already owns the physical Galaxy camera, logarithmic native travel and floating-origin frame semantics; direct scale must reuse this controller state rather than create another camera or tween loop.

OpenSpace exposes focus-relative navigation and distance operations, supporting a normalized input coordinate that changes distance to one retained focus instead of starting unrelated discrete view transitions.

The installed camera-controls instance already executes the continuous System→Surface product coordinate and defines the viewport-aware System endpoint inherited from the native YEIS entry orientation.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the merged #81 pinned-YEIS current-system LOD and CameraController authority as the full Galaxy-side spatial solution.
Keep the existing single R3F Canvas and renderer lifecycle; only scale-progress data crosses the Galaxy/System ownership boundary.
Compose the restored native LOD executor with the existing normalized product scale coordinator; both authorities already exist and no new transition subsystem is required.
Retain the existing System endpoint framing and native-entry quaternion inheritance so coordinate 1 is the same visible composition on both sides.

candidates.reason: Already validates immediate small-delta motion, exact reversal, semantic boundary crossing and higher-priority takeover; extend the same normalized input semantics upward without giving camera-controls Galaxy authority.

candidates.reason: Visual LOD continuity is good, but a single wheel notch still starts a time-driven full 0→1 trip; user input does not continuously own scale distance and cannot proportionally scrub/reverse the same path.

candidates.name: Project-owned second Galaxy camera/tween executor
candidates.reason: Duplicates CameraController and risks breaking the exact floating-origin/frame-switch semantics that #81 just restored.

decision.rationale: Retain #81's native system LOD, physical-system span, frame switching and System entry orientation unchanged. Extend the normalized product scale coordinate to Galaxy=0 and feed its 0→1 progress into a narrow executor inside YeisGalaxyScene. The existing YEIS CameraController remains the only Galaxy camera state; it is positioned along a captured focus-relative logarithmic path, while BodyRenderer/BodyPoints/OrbitLines keep providing native visual LOD. Coordinate 1 hands off through the already matched System overview. Reverse System→Galaxy remounts the retained native view and evaluates the same path backward. No new renderer, camera, router, target database, fade or RAF-owned animation is introduced.
decision.fallback: For a target that cannot resolve to a native stellar frame, retain the existing discrete product fallback rather than fabricate a second physical scale model.
